label: r4c1
name: Flip-only big batch + stem skip
hypothesis: r3c2 recipe plus the r3c3 stem skip. The footprint head also gets the flipped, unblurred per-cell stem features, so pooled max and min can match landing layers to missing cells more sharply. Large batches should keep both seeds stable. Refuted if the mean is no higher than 0.823, or if either seed drops clearly below 0.80.
last_analysis: The key finding is alignment. Any version that keeps the unflipped stem (RowMix, Mixer, concat of flipped and unflipped, or a flip only in the head) collapsed to immediate DONE in most seeds. Mirroring the learned stem features along X before the 3x3 convolutions (flip-only) made both seeds escape the collapse in every run, so later layers work in landing coordinates. With 128 envs and 2,048-sample batches, r3c2 reached 0.844 and 0.803 (mean 0.823). The small-batch run of the same network (r3c1) spread from 0.26 to 0.80, so larger batches seem to reduce seed luck. The stem skip to the head (r3c3, 0.62 against 0.53 at small batch) is within noise but may help. Training success was still rising at the end of every run, so learning is short of samples and the network should stay small. In this last round each candidate refines r3c2 with one change: the stem skip, longer credit assignment (gamma and GAE lambda), or 3 PPO epochs to collect more samples.
